subject.title: refactor(ios): simplify node and Watch lifecycle ownership

question: After real simulator or device evidence is attached, should the iOS owners accept this split of node-model, Watch, and notification lifecycle responsibilities?
rationale: The `maintainer` label and behavior-sensitive ownership split require a human decision about the intended iOS boundary; automated tests alone cannot establish that the resulting live lifecycle is the preferred design.

options.title: Request live iOS proof first
options.body: Ask for redacted simulator/device output or runtime logs that exercise approval readback, Watch correlation, and notification timeout behavior before making the ownership decision.

options.title: Accept after internal owner validation
options.body: An iOS owner may accept the refactor after independently validating the same lifecycle paths in a simulator or device environment.

recommendation.title: Request live iOS proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted simulator/device output or runtime logs that exercise approval readback, Watch correlation, and notification timeout behavior before making the ownership decision.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the current lifecycle split and its focused coverage; broader current-main ownership evidence was unavailable in the supplied context.
